belief: If I lose this job, I lose everything.
origins: When a household depends on one income, or when a job has also given us our identity, friends, and purpose, the thought of losing it can feel like the end. Past layoffs, an unstable family history, or a workplace that keeps people anxious can add to the fear. Some of the risk is real, and planning is wise, but the belief that we would lose everything can drive anxiety and poor decisions now.
teaches: Scripture does not pretend that loss cannot come. But Paul writes that nothing in all creation, neither death nor life, nor the present nor the future, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus. God says do not fear, for I am with you; I will strengthen you and help you. The psalmist says that though a righteous person falls, he will not be overwhelmed, for the Lord is holding his hand. A job can be lost. Our standing with God, our family, and our faith cannot.
self_statements: If this job ends, my life is over.
I would lose my home, my friends, and my future.
I cannot take any risk at work.
I must say yes to everything to stay safe.
There is nothing else for me out there.
errors: Jumping from job loss to total ruin.
Predicting disaster before anything has happened.
Believing that I either keep this job or lose everything.
Forgetting the skills, people, and options I have.
questions: What exactly would I lose, and what would I still have?
What skills, experience, and relationships would I keep?
Have I faced job uncertainty before, and what happened?
What is my plan if the worst occurred, even in outline?
What can I do now to be a little more prepared?
What can never be taken from me?
truth: A job loss would be hard, but it would not be the loss of everything. God, my family, my faith, and my abilities would remain. I can plan wisely and prepare without letting fear run my life.
hw_truths: Nothing can separate me from God’s love.
A job loss is a hard event, not the end of my life.
I have skills and people that stay with me.
God holds my hand when I fall.
Planning is wise; panic is not.
I can take one preparation step now.
log: Each week, write what you would keep if the job ended and one preparation step you took.
actions: Write faith, family, skills, character, and experience.
Write a simple what-if plan: who you would call, what you would update, and what you would cut first.
Do one small preparation step this month.
Read it aloud and name your fear to God.
prayer: Father, You know my fear about losing this job. Hold me, remind me that nothing can separate me from Your love, and help me plan with wisdom instead of panic. Amen.
hw_questions: What skills and people do I have?
What has God done in past uncertainty?
What can never be taken from me?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Nothing can separate me from God’s love, so a job loss would not be the loss of everything.”
